A1.justification: Both PDFs describe UniGame and contain readable main text, equations, tables, figures, and Appendices A–G. Content can be matched reliably despite extensive reformatting and figure renumbering.

before.justification: v1 reports original benchmark evaluations, component ablations, robustness results, backbone experiments, and training-dynamics analyses.

after.justification: v3 retains these original empirical results and adds perturber-depth, buffer-capacity, and additional-backbone evaluations.

M1.justification: The decoder-constrained perturber, semantic filtering, hard-example replay, losses, and alternating updates remain unchanged in Section 3 and Algorithm 1. The additional capacity experiments test variants without changing the selected three-layer perturber or 50-image buffer.

E1.justification: Training and evaluation retain the same datasets and tasks, including VQAv2, CC3M, the understanding/generation benchmarks, NaturalBench, and AdVQA. The additional backbones and smaller training fraction change experimental configurations, not dataset or task coverage.

E2.justification: BLIP-3o and Chameleon already appeared as cross-model baselines in v1, but v3 adds comparisons with their own UniGame-trained counterparts in Section 4.6 and Appendix C.1. Comparator membership in the existing benchmark tables and embedding-perturbation ablation remains unchanged.

E3.justification: New backbone validations use a 0.4 fraction of the VQAv2 training set. New capacity experiments vary perturber depth and buffer size. These introduce additional experimental configurations; the original splits, metrics, training settings, and consistency-score formula remain unchanged.

E4.justification: Section 4.4 adds sensitivity tests comparing two-, three-, and four-layer perturbers and buffers holding 10, 30, or 50 images. These provide limited additional evidence about capacity choices. Existing component, learning-rate, perturbation, robustness, convergence, and case-study analyses are retained.

E5.justification: The reporting of statistical uncertainty is unchanged, including the existing shaded perturbation-sensitivity plot. The added experiments report point estimates without introducing run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, or significance tests.

E6.justification: New capacity comparisons report 82.8/83.4/81.2% for two/three/four-layer perturbers and 82.5/83.1/83.4% for buffers of 10/30/50 images. Appendix C.1 adds backbone results, including reported consistency gains of 2.5 for BLIP-3o and 2.2 for Chameleon. Existing table values and plotted findings are retained; the added backbone results use separate partial-training conditions.

T1.justification: The mathematical objectives and Appendix G assumptions, propositions, proof sketch, gradient-regularization derivation, and manifold-expansion lemma are unchanged. Equation reformatting does not alter their substance.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same self-adversarial framework, architecture-generality claims, and headline improvements. Explicitly identifying GenEval for the +0.02 generation improvement clarifies an existing claim rather than changing its scope.

C2.justification: v3 interprets the new capacity results as favoring moderate perturber expressiveness and greater buffer diversity. It also adds a data-ratio rationale for the unchanged 0.6/0.4 consistency-score weighting. Existing mechanism explanations and limitations remain substantially unchanged.

D1.justification: The advertised code location changes from AIFrontierLab/UniGame to AIFrontierLab/TorchUMM. v3 documents the training fraction for its added backbone experiments, while retaining the original optimizer, precision, hardware, architecture, and replay settings. Repository availability cannot be established from the PDFs.

R1.justification: Both versions retain the same 46 cited works and positioning relative to reconstruction alignment, reward-based post-training, adversarial training, and GANs. Citation ordering and page references change without substantive research repositioning.

P1.justification: The narrative and section sequence largely persist. Changes include localized wording edits, the added backbone-validation subsection, acknowledgments, a corresponding-author note, and removal of the final draft warning. There is no extensive prose rewrite.

P2.justification: The document changes throughout from a single-column report to a two-column layout, substantially resizing and redistributing figures and tables. v1 Figure 6 is separated into v3 Figures 6 and 7, with revised captions and subsequent renumbering. The underlying visual evidence is retained.

improvement.justification: The new capacity ablations strengthen the justification for existing design choices, and the BLIP-3o/Chameleon evaluations provide additional evidence for architectural generality beyond v1's principal Janus-Pro experiments and existing extensions. These are useful but limited gains: the added backbone reporting is brief, uncertainty reporting is unchanged, and the main findings and acknowledged limitations persist.
